[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Object disposal tasks should be handled as a verified pick-and-place sequence. First, locate the specified object (the pencil) on the table; before searching, confirm that the object exists or is likely present, and if the exact instance is unavailable, explore alternatives or retry instead of stopping. Pick up the object and verify the action succeeded. Next, locate the target container (the trash can); if the first search fails, search for other valid instances or alternatives. Then move toward the trash can while checking for obstacles along the path, since blocked movement can fail even if prior moves succeeded; if blocked, replan around or away from the obstruction. Finally, execute put_down to place the pencil in the trash can and verify environmental feedback confirms success rather than assuming it worked.

## Preliminary Thinking
1) Search for and locate the pencil on the table, exploring nearby surfaces or other object instances if the first search fails. 2) Pick up the pencil carefully and securely, then verify the pick_up succeeded. 3) Search for and locate the trash can, exploring alternative trash cans or valid receptacles if the first search fails. 4) Move toward the trash can while checking that the path is clear; if an obstacle blocks movement, replan by changing direction or navigating around it. 5) Put the pencil into the trash can with put_down or the appropriate disposal action. 6) Verify the action succeeded and that the pencil is actually in the trash can before concluding the task.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
